a volume-stimulated, K∶Cl cotransport which is highly expressed in the young red cells of normal individuals and in those with sickle cell anemias.
the characterization of a K+ efflux which is activated in red cell swelling.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the NEM-stimulation K+ efflux in young AA and SS red cells is highly dependent on cell volume, and the interindividual variation in the SS cells may be a factor contributing to the clinical variability of sickle cell disease.
the volume-stimulated, NEM-sensitive, K∶Cl flux in young red cells from AA and SS individuals is highly expressed and that this flux is not cell-age dependent in AA or SS cells.

a Cl−/K+ exchange is highly active in the young red cells of AA and SS individuals and that it is activated by cell swelling, an event which may have pathophysiology relevance.
